name: Accessory dwelling unit (ADU)
summary: Backyard or attached second unit on an existing single-family lot. Per-SF cost is high ($150–400/SF), because a full kitchen, bath and utility service are spread over only 400–900 SF and projects are one-offs with tight site access. Utility connections, especially new meters and long trenches, are the biggest swing items. The evidence is owner surveys from California and Portland, which report all-in cost including design and permits, plus 2026 contractor ranges. There is no national government benchmark, so confidence is medium-low.

typicalSize.method: ADUs are built one per lot. California allows an ADU plus a JADU, hence the high of 2.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Portland owner data (e2): average detached new construction 676 SF, garage conversion 504 SF, attached 556 SF, above-garage 978 SF. Mid ≈ detached average, rounded down; low/high span conversions to above-garage units.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Many states (e.g., CA, OR, WA) restrict ADU parking mandates; typically none required. Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: = perSF × sfPerPrimaryUnit for a detached new-construction ADU: mid $275 × 650 ≈ $180k; low $175 × 450 ≈ $80k (conversions, prefab shells); high $400 × 900 = $360k. Cross-checks: Block Renovation 2026 national all-in totals of $150k–$400k+ for detached and $50k–$150k for garage conversions (e3); Terner 2020 CA median $150k all-in (e1); Portland 2016–19 detached average $180,833 all-in (e2).

perSF.method: Evidence years are mixed: 2016–19 (e2), 2020 (e1), 2026 (e3), labeled 2026 because the range is set from the 2026 source. Block Renovation 2026 national range is $150–400/SF (e3), with its examples at $275/SF for 800 SF and $350/SF for 500 SF. Older owner-survey medians are all-in: CA $250/SF (e1) and Portland detached $305/SF (e2). Removing ~15–20% design/permit/utility soft cost gives ~$205–255 hard in their years, consistent with ~$250–300 after 2020–26 escalation. Mid $275 = the Block 800 SF example and the center of the escalated survey values. Low $175 is above Block's $150 floor because conversions reuse shell/foundation and are better modeled with low SF. High $400 = Block's ceiling.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC general conditions and OH&P for the ADU and work on the host lot (foundation, utility trenching from the main house of typical length, small hardscape). Excludes design/engineering, permit and impact fees, utility-company meter/connection charges (see line items), long utility runs, furniture and land.

qualityTiers.method: Economy = low/mid (175/275 ≈ 0.64), representing conversions and prefab kits. Premium ≈ Block's $350/SF small-unit example (e3) / 275 ≈ 1.27. Luxury is judgment (custom design, high-cost metros).

systemSplit.method: Derived from the single-family split (NAHB 2024 Table 1 mapped to CSI). Adjustments, all judgment: Div 01 up to 15% (small one-off project, mobilization and tight access); 22 and 26 up (full kitchen and bath plus a new electrical sub-panel/service over few SF); 33 at 4% (utility trenching from the main house); 32 down (little landscaping/paving); 04 and 05 minimal.

lineItems.name: Separate electric meter/service from utility

cost.method: High = SDG&E's required new-ADU meter at 'roughly $10,500' (e4, CA-SanDiego). Low/mid are judgment for utilities that allow a sub-meter or cheaper service drop.

lineItems.notes: Some utilities require a separate meter for new detached ADUs.

lineItems.name: Separate water meter / service

cost.method: High = Austin example 'a separate water meter can run around $30,000' (e4, TX-Austin). Low/mid are judgment, as many cities allow a shared meter.

lineItems.notes: Only where the water utility requires a separate meter.

lineItems.name: Extra-long utility trenching (far rear-lot siting)

cost.method: Block Renovation: utility trenching for far-off sites 'can easily add $15,000–$30,000' (e4).

lineItems.notes: Typical-length laterals are already in the baseline.

lineItems.name: Slope/access, tree removal and soils allowance

cost.method: Block Renovation: slope/access 'an additional $5,000–$15,000'; soil/foundation '$5,000–$15,000 or more'; large tree removal '$2,000–$4,000' (e4). High ≈ the sum of the high ends.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Block Renovation: furnishing a one-bedroom ADU 'typically costs around $8,000–$10,000' (e4). Mid = midpoint; low/high widened.

pctOfHard.method: Design and engineering 'typically run 10–15% of total ADU construction cost' (e4). Permits and impact fees run $1,500–$25,000 by municipality (≈1–14% of a $180k hard cost), with Seattle permitting alone at $20k–40k (e4). Mid 20% = design 12% + permits/fees 6% + survey/misc 2%. Portland all-in owner figures include design, permits and utility connections (e2), consistent with ~15–20%.

softCosts.notes: Pre-approved city plans can cut design cost by up to 40% (Block Renovation). Many states cap or waive impact fees for ADUs under 750 SF (e.g., California).

hard.method: Judgment: existing-lot unknowns (buried utilities, soils, access), one-off small contractors.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low: conversion at ~$60k hard + 12% soft. High: Seattle/LA detached ADUs, which Block Renovation reports at $300k–$500k all-in (e3), plus headroom.

source.title: Implementing the Backyard Revolution: Perspectives of California's ADU Owners (blog synopsis)
source.publisher: Terner Center for Housing Innovation, UC Berkeley

evidence.quote: The median statewide construction cost of an ADU is $150,000, or $250/square foot (sf).
evidence.scopeNotes: Owner survey published April 2021; the data year is assumed to be 2020 (not stated). Owner-reported cost, likely including design/permits. All ADU types pooled. Also: 71% of ADUs cost under $200,000.

source.title: Calculating The Costs of Building an ADU

evidence.quote: Detached new construction: average cost $180,833, average size 676 sq ft, $305/sq ft ... These costs include design costs, permit costs, utility connection costs, and all construction costs.
evidence.scopeNotes: Self-reported owner costs, 2016–2019 projects (dataYear = latest year). Other types: basement $265/SF, attached $300/SF (556 SF), garage conversion $297/SF (504 SF), above-garage $212/SF (978 SF). Landscaping and furniture are excluded. Small samples.

source.title: A Deep Dive Into ADU Construction Costs: What the Per-Square-Foot Numbers Don't Tell You

evidence.quote: expect to pay $150 to $400 per square foot ... a 500 sq ft detached ADU might come in at $350 per square foot, while an 800 sq ft unit could land at $275 per square foot
evidence.scopeNotes: Contractor/marketplace guide dated April 2026. Totals by type: detached $150,000–$400,000+; garage conversion $50,000–$150,000; prefab $80,000–$250,000+. Metro totals: LA detached $300k–450k+, Seattle $300k–500k, Denver $230k–310k.

source.title: A Deep Dive Into ADU Construction Costs: What the Per-Square-Foot Numbers Don't Tell You

evidence.quote: SDG&E now requires all new construction ADUs to have a separate electric meter at a cost of roughly $10,500 ... In Austin, a separate water meter can run around $30,000.
evidence.scopeNotes: The same page gives: design/engineering 10–15% of construction; permits/impact fees $1,500–$25,000; trenching $15,000–$30,000; slope $5,000–$15,000; furnishing $8,000–$10,000.

openQuestions: No national government ADU cost series. City permit-valuation data (Los Angeles, Seattle and Portland ADU dashboards) and a newer Terner Center statewide survey would firm up the per-SF range.
Conversion and detached ADUs differ ~2× in total cost; the engine may want an ADU-type selector rather than one type.
